title: Generating Construction Process Maps with a Large Language Model: On the Road to Practical Use
content: The technological process map, a construction-specific form of the ASME flow process chart, records the works of a construction site in their technological sequence together with the transports, inspections, delays and storages that schedules omit. Although valued in teaching, it is rarely drawn in practice because it is slow to produce. This paper examines whether a general-purpose large language model can generate the map from tender documents that describe the product and its requirements rather than the construction process as a sequence, and whether the project documentation, the bill of quantities or both is the input that determines the result. For ten road construction tenders of one public client, the same model generated a map three times, zero-shot, from each of these three inputs. An independent LLM agent matched the ninety maps step by step, and the differences between inputs were judged against the variation between repeated generations from the same input. Maps built from the bill of quantities were about 40% larger than maps built from the documentation alone, while adding the documentation to the bill changed the map only slightly more than two repeated generations from the same input differed. All measures are structural and do not assess correctness, which is the subject of the expert validation that follows. The results identify the bill of quantities as the input to start from and provide the material for that validation.
